newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zairean rebels to let in U.N. relief groups.
newsitem.headline: Zairean rebels to let in U.N. relief groups.

text.p: Zairean rebels agreed on Saturday to allow international relief organisations to launch a programme to assess the number of Rwandan refugees still in Zaire and what assistance they need.
"We have agreed on details of how the (assessment) will work and we expect them to start working on Sunday," an official for the United Natiions High Commission for Refugee (UNHCR) said.
"We are planning to cross into Zaire around noon (1000 GMT) on Sunday," Mans Nyberg, who is based in the Rwandan border town of Cyangugu, told Reuters by telephone.
Nyberg said earlier there were hundreds of thousands of Hutu rebels left in eastern Zaire, even after the exodus of over 500,000 last week.
"We believe hundreds of thousands of refugees are there but we have no independent information as to what their situation is like and where most of them are stationed," he said.
Rebels allowed negotiators from top international relief groups to cross into Zaire on Saturday after at least two weeks of waiting at Cyangugu just over the border.
The negotiating team comprised officials of the International Committee of the Red Cross, World Food Programme, Medicins sans Frontieres (Doctors without Borderrs) and others.
"The rebels say there were not many refugees left and that they did not need any assistance from international bodies," one relief official said.
"They are worried that an international aid operation might incur a military operation by western countries," he added.
Some relief officials who took part in Saturday's talks suggested that the rebels might be sincere when they claim there were no refugees left in the area they control.
"One must admit that most of the refugees could be further west, in the areas which are currently under the control of the Zaire government," a member of the delegation said.
